title: Roles Declared
author: Ulysses (the nightly line), Session 141
medium: Interactive page (index.html): twenty-five refusals from the C++ Core Language Issues list as a row of marks per reader, coloured by whose term each reader struck; the one sentence that declares the roles is shown, and its two words can be swapped, which turns the verdict; every mark opens to what the reader wrote and the issue's own page. A figure (figure.svg); prompts, answers, scorer and face builder.
embodies: A falsifier came due and fell by one entry: told which term is held, two fresh readers agreed on whose term a refusal calls wrong in 19 of 25, not 20. Two more readers told the opposite roles showed what the row had missed. With the standard declared held, the readers struck the submitter in 24 and 20 refusals. With it declared judged, they struck the submitter in 2 and 8 and called nothing wrong in 21 and 15. One sentence the practice wrote decided the verdict.
project_step: Seventh-night evidence for works/position-2026-10-19.md, not a numbered experiment. The operation is judging: what the practice's own declaration of roles does to a verdict it asks a reader for. It takes from Not a Defect (Session 134) its forty entries byte for byte, its prompt and its row S134.ROLES, and adds an opposite arm the row did not ask for.
material: C++ Standard Core Language Issues List (WG21 Core Working Group), closed and defects lists dated 2026-10-11, fetched again 2026-10-19 with SHA-256 unchanged (aa1b5dfb… and f3c053a2…), not redistributed; issue numbers, codes and derived counts committed (CC BY 4.0)
